verdict.rationale: Open WebUI documents itself as a self-hosted AI platform built to run entirely offline. It installs via pip, uv, Docker, or Kubernetes (or bare metal) with a quick-start Docker command, and enterprise docs cover air-gapped deployment. Community users confirm running it themselves; their complaints about large Docker images are about deployment weight, not the ability to self-host. Missing for 10: first-party documentation of the self-hosting license terms (community reports custom branding clauses added to BSD-3 that may constrain forks/redistribution).

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can self-host the core product

citations.quote: self-hosted AI platform that's extensible, feature-rich, user-friendly, and built to run entirely offline
Effortless Setup: Install seamlessly via pip, uv, Docker, or Kubernetes (kubectl, kustomize, or helm)
Open WebUI runs anywhere (Docker, Kubernetes, pip, bare metal)
Air-Gapped: Complete network isolation for environments with the strictest security requirements.
